SiteMinder’s channel-manager page illustrates the channel-management bottleneck: it connects hotel inventory with OTAs and distribution channels, PMS/RMS systems, payment processing and hotel apps. SiteMinder is ASX-listed, so it is useful as context but excluded from the US-listed candidate list.

memory_update.text: AGYS is the cleanest US-listed pure-play candidate for the hospitality operating-stack node because its product set directly spans PMS, POS, inventory/procurement, payments and guest-journey software.

PAR is a smaller-cap restaurant operating-stack candidate with relevant POS, ordering, loyalty, payments and back-office exposure; survival to later layers depends on verifying ARR quality, integration execution and liquidity/free-cash-flow path.
FOUR should be used as a payments reference asset rather than the main underfollowed alpha candidate; verify hospitality/restaurant vertical mix and organic payment-volume growth.

PFGC expands the node beyond software into restaurant/hospitality procurement and distribution; it is a second-order beneficiary candidate where fill rates, route density and order completeness may be the true operating bottleneck.
US-listed hotel channel-manager pure plays appear scarce; ASX-listed SiteMinder is a strong context anchor but cannot enter the US-listed universe except as non-US reference evidence.

summary: Expanded the US-listed universe around the hospitality and travel operating stack with an underfollowed discovery lens. The most relevant small/mid-cap candidates cluster around hotel property-management/POS/procurement software, restaurant operating software, hospitality payments, and foodservice distribution/procurement. Mega-cap reference anchors such as Oracle Hospitality, Booking/Expedia, large hotel chains, and OTAs are useful for context but were not prioritized because this pass is focused on obscure or second-order public assets.
